criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a_result_whose_totals_disagree_with_model_usage_is_flagged_end_to_end passes. It builds the record from a result event with modelUsage for the requested model and a total_cost_usd that differs from the per-model costUSD sum. It uses the same parse and record-building helper as the positive test. It asserts, before calling check_invocation, that the record's reported total differs from the modelUsage sum. It then asserts exactly one Reconciliation violation whose detail names the per-model cost sum.
criteria.evidence: The test passed in both runs. In invocation.rs (lines 435-450), `DISAGREEING` has `total_cost_usd` 0.75, and its `modelUsage` has a claude-sonnet-5-5 entry with `costUSD` 0.10 and a claude-haiku-5-5 entry with 0.20. The test calls `record_from` (the same helper as the positive test) and asserts that `models_used` contains MODEL and that the reported total differs from the per-model sum by more than 0.01. Only then does it call `check_invocation`. It asserts `found.len()==1` and that the detail contains "per-model costs sum", which matches the message at reconcile.rs:73.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: the positive test a_result_whose_top_level_usage_includes_a_subagent_reconciles_end_to_end still passes. The job 2fsa top-level usage 90/52656/3634696/134508 differs from the modelUsage of 6/3136/275219/3821, the record carries the modelUsage tokens, and check_invocation returns no violations.
criteria.evidence: The test passed. The `AGREEING` fixture has top-level usage 90/134508/3634696/52656 and a sonnet `modelUsage` entry of 6/3821/275219/3136. The test asserts that `measured_tokens` equals [6,3821,275219,3136] and that `check_invocation` returns `vec![]`.

criteria.criterion: The negative test has no case that edits a built record by hand and calls it end-to-end. Any such case is labelled a gate-only check. The doc comments on the test and the fixtures state that token disagreement cannot arise through the parser under the modelUsage definition.
criteria.evidence: The negative test has no hand-edited record; its new doc comment says "No record is edited by hand." The doc comments on the `DISAGREEING` fixture and on the test both say a token disagreement cannot arise through the parser under the `modelUsage` definition.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md records the fix and the modelUsage definition. It states honestly which disagreement the end-to-end negative test covers.
criteria.evidence: The CHANGELOG diff adds the `modelUsage` definition and says the end-to-end negative test "covers only the cost disagreement (`total_cost_usd` against the `costUSD` sum)" and that a token disagreement is not claimed to be covered.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: all pass and are clean, including the existing stream, claude, gate and landing tests.
criteria.evidence: Every test binary reported ok with 0 failed. Clippy finished with no warnings, and `cargo fmt --check` printed nothing.

findings.summary: The docs say a token disagreement cannot arise through the parser, but they don't mention the fallback to top-level usage.
findings.evidence: In stream.rs (lines 35-44), `requested_usage` returns `self.usage` (the top-level usage) when `modelUsage` has no entry for the model. In that case `check_invocation` still reports a token-related Reconciliation violation ("no usage for the requested model", reconcile.rs:95). The accepted reading asked the test and changelog to state this "unless the parser falls back" caveat; the new text does not.

findings.summary: The claim that the test fails with the cost check disabled was not independently confirmed.
findings.evidence: Confirming it would mean editing reconcile.rs, which the verifier role may not do. The test's assertions (exactly one violation whose detail contains "per-model costs sum") would fail if the cost check were removed, so the claim is plausible from reading the code.

summary: The change passes. The negative test `a_result_whose_totals_disagree_with_model_usage_is_flagged_end_to_end` builds its record through the same path as the positive test: `record_from` → `StreamState::on_line` → `output_from_result` → `invocation_record`. The input really is bad: `total_cost_usd` is 0.75 while the per-model `costUSD` values sum to 0.30. The test checks that the input is bad before it calls `check_invocation`. It then requires exactly one Reconciliation violation whose detail contains "per-model costs sum". That rules out the "no usage for the requested model" branch. The candidate changes only doc comments and CHANGELOG.md, and it now states plainly that the end-to-end negative test covers only the cost disagreement. I ran `cargo test` (all pass, including both end-to-end tests), `cargo clippy --all-targets` (clean) and `cargo fmt --check` (clean). One minor point: the docs say a token disagreement "cannot arise through the parser", but they don't mention that `requested_usage` falls back to the top-level usage when the requested model has no `modelUsage` entry, which the accepted reading asked them to say. I could not confirm the producer's claim that the test fails with the cost check disabled, because my role may not edit code.
